idiom_name: Play session (play.api.mvc.Session) - a signed, unencrypted cookie carried on every request
implementation_notes: Play's Session is this pattern built into the framework: the data is not stored on the server but added to each subsequent request through a cookie (PLAY_SESSION by default), limited to roughly 4 KB and to string values into which JSON can be serialized, and the content is visible to the browser - signing prevents modification, not disclosure. Because the session is just an HTTP header, a modification is only visible to the next request, which is why Play pairs withSession with a redirect; play.http.session.maxAge adds a functional timeout (and sets the JWT exp claim), and cookieName plus the security settings configure scope. Use http4s-style middleware or an encrypted token when the state must be hidden or must travel outside a browser.
pitfalls: Signed, not encrypted: session content is visible to the browser, so Play's own documentation warns against sensitive data in it.
Values are strings capped by the ~4 KB cookie limit, so serialized JSON eats the budget quickly.
Changes apply only to the next request - reading the session after withSession in the same request returns the old value, the documented reason to redirect after modifying it.
Without play.http.session.maxAge there is no functional timeout (the session expires when the browser closes), even though the cookie carries a JWT exp claim.
